messages.subject: dwish as covariance matrix
parts:
hello everyone,
I would like to use a prior distribution dwish for a covariance matrix that I then use in dmnorm distribution.
But it is not working and I have the following error :
ConfModel <- configureMCMC(Model, thin = Thin, monitors = params)
Error in .Object$initialize(...) : 
  At present, the NIMBLE MCMC does not provide a sampler for non-conjugate Wishart nodes. Users can implement an appropriate sampling algorithm as a nimbleFunction, for use in the MCMC.

Here is my first priori attempt 
    covar0[1:n_species,1:n_species]~dwish(ID[1:n_species,1:n_species], df=n_species)
Then used in : 
   for (site in 1:n_sites) {
      Sp.resp[site,1:n_species] ~ dmnorm(mean=meanDmnorm[1:n_species], cov=covar0[1:n_species,1:n_species])
    }
    
But the dwish output does not seems symmetrical (what is it form ?), so I tried changing it :
    covar0[1:n_species,1:n_species]~dwish(ID[1:n_species,1:n_species], df=n_species)

    for (i in 1:n_species){
      for (j in 1:n_species){
        covar[i,j]<-covar0[max(i,j),min(i,j)]
      }
    }

And use covar instead of covar0 in the dmnorm but the result is the same.
Any ideas ? Or exemple on how to use a covariance matrix done by wishart ditribution in dmnorm ?


Thank you in advance.

messages.author: c9e9cbbfb3b043f0
messages.subject: Re: dwish as covariance matrix
parts:
Ugoline, thanks for sending your question out.

The short answer, is that due to constraints on Wishart-distributed (multivariate) random variables, sampling from Wishart distributions is non-trivial.  At present, the NIMBLE MCMC only has a sampler provided for *conjugate* Wishart nodes.  The common conjugacy case is where the Wishart-distributed node appears as the *precision* matrix of a multivariate normal distribution.  (in your case, you're using it as the *covariance* matrix, thus it's not conjugate).  That's what the error message is attempting to say, that we do not provide a sampler (yet) for non-conjugate Wishart nodes.

An example of using a *conjugate* Wishart node, which would work in the MCMC:

    code <- nimbleCode( {
        Omega[1:M,1:M] ~ dwish(R[1:M,1:M], 4)
        for(i in 1:N) {
            Y[i, 1:M] ~ dmnorm(mu[1:M], Omega[1:M,1:M])
        }
    })

This works because the *default parameterization of the dnmorn is in terms of the precision matrix*.  You could do exactly the same thing by explicitly naming the precision matrix argument:

    code <- nimbleCode( {
        Omega[1:M,1:M] ~ dwish(R[1:M,1:M], 4)
        for(i in 1:N) {
            Y[i, 1:M] ~ dmnorm(mu[1:M], prec = Omega[1:M,1:M])
        }
    })

Does this answer your question?
